algorithm.title: Evaluation and Treatment of the Patient with Suspected Thoracic Outlet Syndrome.

cell.label: Physical examination shows severe neurologic signs, muscle wasting, or venous or arterial blockage?
Refer for specialty evaluation and management.
Two or more provocative maneuvers positive (see ).
Evaluate further with chest and cervical x-rays to rule out cervical rib or bony lesion. Abnormality relating to symptoms seen on plain film?
Symptoms mild, position dependent, and tolerable?

Consult with specialty service for further management. Consider alternative diagnoses. Consider addition of the following: (1) Advanced imaging with MRI of the cervicothoracic spine from C4 to T5. (2) Electrodiagnostic studies to assist with ruling out alternative diagnoses. (3) Upper extremity Doppler study for evaluation of vascular symptoms. (4) Anterior scalene block to evaluate symptom relief and potential for surgical correction.
Refer for conservative treatment with 6-8 wk of physical therapy. Relief of symptoms?

footnotes.footnote: Signs and symptoms Neurological: numbness, pain, and paresthesias usually in ulnar nerve distribution. Possible atrophy of the abductor pollicis brevis, interossei, and hypothenar muscles. Venous: upper extremity swelling, fatigue, venous distention, and cyanosis. Arterial: upper extremity pallor, claudication, fatigue, coolness, and possible ulcerations. Symptoms increase with repeated upper extremity use, overhead activities, carrying motions, and motions that stretch the brachial plexus.
